original_test_intent: Redo PCIe transmitter equalization exactly 10,000 times on the mapped link and prove every redo completes the approved equalization trajectory and returns to the required generation and width without new lane, link, endpoint, GPU, host, or platform errors.
original_method: Pin the LTSSM Tx-equalization-redo operation, complete path and lane map, generation/width, equalization phase and preset/coefficient rules, timing, transient allowance, and error contract; baseline link/equalization/health; durably record each numbered redo request, phase/status, negotiated state, lane result, deadline, and error deltas before the next redo; stop on first anomaly and recover out of band.
manual_activity: Owner/FAE approves the equalization recipe, per-lane scope, target generation/width, and link-stress risk; an operator isolates the SUT, observes out-of-band state, and owns recovery after a marginal or lost link.
required_inputs: Pinned NVIDIA LTSSM Tx-equalization-redo tool/configuration and compatible firmware/driver
Target generation/width, equalization phases, preset/coefficient ownership, settle deadline, transient, and lane pass rules
10,000-redo count, durable storage, error-delta, abort, final-state, and recovery contract
safety_requirements: Dedicated non-production SUT and explicit 10,000-redo approval
No unsaved workload and verified out-of-band console/recovery
Do not alter presets or coefficients outside the pinned vendor recipe
Stop on failed phase, lane anomaly, timeout, downtraining, endpoint loss, new AER, GPU/host reset, thermal/power anomaly, tool fault, or evidence gap
No counter clearing, blind retry, or continued stress after first fault
agent_execution_scope: Validate exact variant, path/lane mapping, recipe, baseline, interlocks, and ledger
Run only the approved Tx-eq redo operation
Commit phase/lane/equalization/link/deadline/error results before the next redo
Correlate signal-training state with endpoint, GPU, host, BMC, thermal, and power health
Do not use same-code Console/Thermal material, invent coefficients, retry, continue after fault, or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Tx-eq redo recipe, path/lane scope, equalization rules, and 10,000-redo risk
Define generation/width, phase/lane/deadline/transient and error acceptance
Review the complete redo ledger and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The generic loop matches the named operation but lacks the exact LTSSM recipe, link/lane identity, generation/width, equalization semantics, and durable transaction proof; a final lspci/dmesg sweep cannot establish 10,000 successful redos.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the pinned LTSSM Tx-eq redo recipe with an atomic monotonic ledger and a hard interlock preventing redo N+1 until N's phase, lane, negotiated state, deadline, and error results are durable.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: LTSSM, exactly 10,000 Tx Eq Redos, expected width/speed, no errors, no bundle, and 30/1440-minute allocation remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: INTERLOCKED 10,000x PCIE TX EQUALIZATION REDO SOAK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat each redo as a per-lane signal-training transaction with durable phase, negotiated-link, timing, and error evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact variant isolation, path/lane identity, equalization semantics, evidence durability, first-fault handling, and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final full-width link cannot reveal skipped redos, intermittent equalization failures, marginal lanes, temporary downtraining, or earlier AER events.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated equalization can expose or aggravate marginal signal integrity; an uncontrolled recipe can disturb a shared hierarchy, strand the endpoint, or create reset storms.

project_override_considerations: Vendor-defined aggregate pass may be used only if its artifact preserves per-redo and per-lane failure visibility, gap detection, and first-fault chronology. The shared code never permits evidence from row 1977 or 2287 to substitute for this row.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, shared-code separation, and authorization
Pinned tool/configuration plus complete path/per-lane topology and initial link/equalization state
Monotonic 1-10000 lossless redo ledger with per-lane equalization/LTSSM, timing, negotiated link, and disposition
First-fault recovery or clean final link/endpoint/host state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: This row's Master fields and same-row AI review consistently describe Tx equalization. The shared code is an identity hazard already resolved by source row, hash, and variant; unrelated Console/Thermal content is excluded rather than treated as this row's source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Tx-equalization purpose is clear. Proprietary tooling, exact link/lane recipe, acceptance, high-volume evidence, isolation, and recovery are execution prerequisites, not an irreducible static-review blocker.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2121 Wistron-HW-00472-V002 variant a2ad2978391bc10d: approve the pinned LTSSM Tx-equalization-redo recipe, complete root-port/bridge/retimer/endpoint/per-lane map, target generation/width, equalization phases and preset/coefficient ownership, settle/deadline/transient rules, exact 10,000-redo/checkpoint evidence, acceptable lane/AER/error deltas, first-fault interlocks, final state, and out-of-band recovery.

review_improvement: Maintains the 10,000-redo signal-integrity stress while making each per-lane equalization result auditable and preventing shared-code Console or Thermal evidence from contaminating this variant.
independent_technical_reasoning: Tx equalization is a lane-level negotiation process whose phase and coefficient behavior can fail even if the link later reaches an apparently healthy final state. Evidence must therefore bind the exact path and generation to each redo, expose marginal or failed lanes, and record any temporary downtraining or AER delta before another redo can overwrite state. The duplicate code cannot be used as identity; row, variant, and hash are controlling because its other occurrences describe wholly different physical-console and thermal objectives.
